title: Mistral releases improved Large 4 weights with sparse attention and cheaper coding
dek: The downloadable trillion-parameter MoE combines token-level expert routing with sparse context selection; new coding results improve on its October preview.
evidence: Mistral October 29 release, Hugging Face architecture and deployment notes, and cited third-party benchmark results; deployment measurements are vendor-reported
takeaway: Sparse experts reduce active computation, not the memory needed to store a trillion-parameter checkpoint. Open weights change deployment control, but not hardware or license constraints.

sections.title: Context

bullets.detail: Mistral introduced Large 4 through an API preview on October 6. The October 29 event is the first downloadable release of improved weights after further reinforcement learning, not the first announcement of the model.

paragraphs: Preview versus release: Mistral introduced Large 4 through an API preview on October 6. The October 29 event is the first downloadable release of improved weights after further reinforcement learning, not the first announcement of the model.

sections.title: What's new

bullets.detail: The text decoder uses 128 routed feed-forward experts, selecting four plus one shared expert per token. Separately, DeepSeek Sparse Attention selects up to 2,048 previous key positions while multi-head latent attention compresses KV state.

The multimodal checkpoint has roughly 1 trillion total parameters, around 49 billion active in the main model per token, and about 52 billion including embeddings and output layers. It accepts text and images, with a stated 1 million-token context window. FP8, NVFP4 and community GGUF formats are available.

Hugging Face supports Transformers, vLLM and llama.cpp. Its published eight-H200 vLLM recipe serves up to 131,072 tokens of context, below the model's advertised 1 million-token limit. The NVFP4 variant targets Blackwell GPUs.

Low, medium and high reasoning modes share the same weights. The Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License permits modification and commercial use but requires a separate agreement for commercial model-as-a-service offerings.

sections.title: Evidence & limitations

bullets.detail: Mistral reports 41% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, up 13 percentage points from its preview, with 30% fewer output tokens. It reports 48% on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, approximately tied with GLM-5.3 while using 47% fewer tokens per task. These comparisons depend on the evaluated agent configurations.

Mistral reports 51% on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index and 96.6% average refusal on malicious cyber prompts from JailbreakBench, StrongREJECT and AgentHarm. A cyber capability score and a refusal score measure different properties.

On a reported eight-H200 FP8 endpoint, Hugging Face observed about 65 generated tokens per second for a single request and about 480 tokens per second aggregate over 1,000 ShareGPT conversations under load. These are hardware-specific serving measurements, not universal model speed.
The community Q4_K_M GGUF is listed at 635 GB, and the Q2_K at 381 GB. Only a subset of experts computes each token, but the full set of experts must still reside somewhere in the inference system.

sections.title: Key takeaways

bullets.lead: Compute sparsity is not storage sparsity
bullets.detail: Activating roughly 52 billion parameters per token does not make a trillion-parameter model fit in the memory footprint of a dense 52-billion-parameter model.

bullets.lead: Context capacity differs from serving capacity
bullets.detail: A model may advertise a million-token context while a practical deployment supports a smaller window because memory, latency and batching limits still apply.
